statement: The cart, checkout, order confirmation and mini-cart pages are this project's own markup inside the source's page shell. No copy of the source's versions exists.
why: /cart, /Cart, /Checkout, /sslchkout and /myaccount are all under robots Disallow rules in the source's robots.txt. They were never requested and never will be.
measured: scope/capture-queue.json records 3,745 robots-disallowed URLs removed from the frontier and 0 captured; clone/tests/test_storefront.py::test_no_robots_disallowed_path_was_captured asserts it
disposition: declared; the pages say on their face that payment settles against a local sandbox

statement: 1,906 product ids listed in the source's own sitemap answer HTTP 200 with the title 'Products no longer Available'.
why: The sitemap over-claims the catalogue by roughly a third. Verified against the source directly with the tracking parameters stripped, in case canonicalisation was at fault: the clean URL answers the same.
disposition: the clone reproduces the source's behaviour: 200 with that page, not 404

statement: 89 assets the pages reference cannot be fetched because the source itself does not serve them: 66 answer 404, 15 answer 403, 8 answer 406.
why: Dead references in the source's own stylesheets and markup, plus eight product images the image host refuses regardless of Accept header.
measured: every missing asset was probed against the source; 3 that answered 200 were this project's gap and were fetched
disposition: the clone reproduces the absence; references to them are deliberately left unrewritten rather than repointed at a local 404

statement: The 'customers also bought' carousels on product pages are empty in the clone. The source populates them with roughly 38 product thumbnails.
why: They are rendered by Unbxd's third-party recommendation SDK, which is stripped along with every other third-party script.
evidence: observed side by side: source loads 38 images under /productmediumimages on /product?p_id=10145, the clone loads 0
measured: no empty tiles are left visible; the clone's visible-broken-image count is 0, matching the source
disposition: not reproduced; a local recommender would be invention rather than reconstruction

statement: The search results page does not show a result count matching the query; it carries the donor page's count.
why: The number appears 300 times in the donor page and most occurrences are not the count -- they sit inside product ids, prices and asset names. Substituting all of them would corrupt the page to fix a number.
measured: the query itself IS substituted: 24 plain, 1 upper-case and 284 URL-encoded occurrences

why: Each one needs a screenshot of the source at a frozen viewport. This run's capture stored served HTML and assets, not screenshots, and the source is behind a Cloudflare managed challenge that only a headed browser clears.
disposition: a screenshot of the clone cannot stand in: the comparison would compare the clone to itself and report perfect fidelity

statement: The Zoovu product-finder widget renders nothing; its <zoovu-zoe> element stays undefined on the pages that carry it.
why: Zoovu is a third-party guided-selling service. Its script is stripped and there is nothing local to define the element.
disposition: declared; an undefined custom element renders its children and makes no request

statement: Facet, sort and pagination variants of listings are sampled, not enumerated.
why: Every filter combination is its own URL. A per-listing cap consumed 40 pages per batch and added 86; the frontier grew faster than capture drained it.
measured: caps are per facet type: 104 variant pages across 18 facet kinds were kept and 138,548 URLs were left out, all recorded
disposition: deliberate and recorded; the clone implements filtering from its own catalogue rather than replaying captured combinations

statement: 3,289 product pages kept a structured extract rather than their full body.
why: 11,246 verbatim bodies would be 5.6 GB. Product pages publish a complete schema.org Product record, so the catalogue loses nothing.
measured: 600 product bodies retained; 2 product pages published no schema.org block and their full bodies were kept instead
disposition: those products are served from a detail template cut from a real captured product page

statement: Three additional asset origins are treated as local: cdn.prod.website-files.com, d3e54v103j8qbb.cloudfront.net and cdnjs.cloudflare.com.
why: /p/shop/ and /p/resources/ -- 3,328 pages, a third of the site -- are a Webflow build whose stylesheets, scripts and 5,019 product photographs live entirely on Webflow's CDN. Treating them as third parties would have frozen every one of those pages as unstyled HTML with no images, and no closure gate would have reported it: a page with no stylesheet makes no request.
disposition: they are static resource origins the page itself requests; nothing is sent to them and the runtime makes no request to them

statement: The PerimeterX bot-detection sensor is not reproduced. Its first-party path answers a JSON 404 naming it.
why: It is a bot-detection sensor served from a first-party path of two long random segments, so it looks like an ordinary page request.
disposition: declared absent rather than left as an unexplained same-origin 404

statement: 44 category listings render the source's empty-results page.
why: The source renders an invented path and a real-but-empty department identically, with HawkSearch's 'We were unable to find search results for ...' body. It draws no distinction, so neither does the clone.
measured: 44 pages; they are served, not discarded, because that is the site's own empty state

statement: Google Analytics and Tag Manager, proxied by the source through the first-party path /securemetrics/, are removed.
why: A first-party tracker proxy is structurally invisible to a remote-request audit, because the request never leaves the origin.
measured: the path is in the clone's declared-absent set and answers a JSON 404
